newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open flat to 1.00 higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open flat to 1.00 higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open unchanged to 1.00 cent higher Friday, although some traders said producers' decision to loosen up arabica exports could weigh on sentiment.

Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) technical committee decided Thursday to recommend the release of an additional 200,000 bags of arabica coffee to the world market in the first half of 1997.
The technical committee also decided to revoke a previous decision to reduce exports of arabica by 300,000 bags during the same period.
Reaction to the news was mixed. While some market participants said the export increase would ease supply concerns, others claimed it was not enough coffee to relieve the supply crunch.
The ACPC full council is expected to ratify Thursday's decision by the technical committee at a meeting in May in London.

Thursday, Arabica prices ended up, but off highs after the news from an ACPC meeting in London. May coffee rose to a peak of 174.50 cents before closing at 169.15 cents, up 1.05 cents on the day. May reached a low today of 166.00. July rose 2.30, to 157.20, while the back months closed down 0.55 to up 3.50.

After Thursday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks grew for the eleventh day in a row, reaching 70,529 60-kg bags as of March 19. There were an additional 13,850 bags pending grading, the exchange said.
On the charts, May near-term resistance seen at 175.00 cents, with a major upside hurdle seen at 190.00 cents. Support was pegged at 165.50-165.00, then 160.00, traders said.
In London, robusta futures were firmer early Friday on trade buying. At the midday break, May coffee was up $15, to $1,615 a tonne.
